reference_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(t.n_orders), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
alternatives:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n_orders), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM customer_orders

SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL

other_way.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n_orders), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM customer_orders
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step names the per-customer counts first and reads top to bottom; the derived table keeps the step where it is used.
